references.label: APAGBI Fasting 2025
references.citation: Association of Paediatric Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland. Pre-operative fasting position statement (2018) and Hot Topic: Should paediatric patients be allowed to 'sip til send' prior to elective surgery? November 2025.
references.excerpt: The 2018 APAGBI position statement sets the adopted elective pathway for healthy children: at least one hour for clear fluids, three hours for breast milk, and six hours for infant formula and solids. The November 2025 Hot Topic is an evidence review, not a replacement position statement: it recommends that units may offer sip-til-send (non-caloric clear fluids at 3 mL/kg/hour, maximum 150 mL/hour, until call to theatre) within that elective pathway, under local governance and staff training. Delayed gastric emptying, significant reflux, severe obesity, neurological impairment and emergency surgery need individualised plans.
references.reviewNote: Hot Topic states that national work is underway to inform an updated APAGBI position statement; it does not itself replace the 2018 intervals. Applies only to healthy elective children.

references.label: BJA 2011 (Rectus sheath block)

references.excerpt: This study demonstrates that ultrasound-guided RSB provides superior analgesia in the perioperative period compared with infiltration of the surgical site after umbilical hernia repair.

references.label: ERAS Ambulatory 2023
references.citation: Elias KM, Stone AB, Ljungqvist O, Urman RD. Enhanced recovery protocols for ambulatory surgery. Best Practice & Research Clinical Anaesthesiology. 2023;37(3):285-303.
references.excerpt: The ERAS fundamentals for ambulatory surgery are based on five pillars, including (1) preoperative patient counseling, education, and optimization; (2) multimodal and opioid-sparing analgesia; (3) nausea and vomiting, wound infection, and venous thromboembolism prophylaxis; (4) maintenance of euvolemia; and (5) encouragement of early mobility.

cards.question: What BMI is acceptable for day-case surgery?
cards.answer: There is no absolute BMI cutoff. BADS guidance is to assess functional capacity, comorbidity (especially OSA), and surgical complexity rather than weight alone. Many UK units accept BMI up to 50 for appropriate procedures, provided the patient meets all other day-case criteria and a suitable airway plan is in place.

cards.question: When is voiding mandatory before day-case discharge?
cards.answer: After spinal/epidural anaesthesia, inguinal/femoral hernia repair, and perianal/urological surgery — because of the risk of urinary retention. For most other day-case procedures, voiding is not required as long as the patient is well, drinking, and has clear instructions on when to seek help if retention develops.

cards.question: How should a patient with STOP-BANG ≥5 be managed for day surgery?
cards.answer: Stratify as high OSA risk. Use opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia, prefer regional techniques, avoid long-acting sedatives, and monitor for ≥3 h post-op with continuous SpO₂. CPAP-dependent patients should bring their device. Many units admit STOP-BANG ≥5 patients overnight after general anaesthesia.
